final_text:
Both the dashboard and the alert rule now exist in Kibana 9.5.5.

**What the data holds** (`kibana_sample_data_logs`, 14,074 requests)
- Response codes are 200 (12,832), 404 (801), and 503 (441). The only 5xx code present is 503, about 3% of traffic.
- Traffic comes from 1,001 unique client IPs. The top destination countries are CN, IN, US, ID, and BR.
- Timestamps run from 2026-09-27 to 2026-11-26, so part of the data is in the future relative to today (2026-10-10).

**Dashboard: "EFF-5914afda Web logs overview"** (ID `1a509cae-e723-4e8a-8ddb-9c85b3856988`)
- Four metric panels: total requests, 5xx responses, unique client IPs, and average response size.
- Three charts: requests over time, requests by response code, and top 10 destination countries.
- I set the dashboard time range to 2026-09-01 through 2026-12-31 so it covers the sample data. The default "last 15 minutes" would show nothing useful. This is my choice; change it if you want a different window.

**Alert rule: "EFF-5914afda 5xx spike"** (ID `3d68f2bc-10e9-4154-9478-cae2dd1ab95a`)
- Type: Elasticsearch query rule on `kibana_sample_data_logs`, enabled.
- Runs every 1 minute. Matches `response.keyword` from "500" through "599", counted over a 5-minute window. Fires when the count is greater than 10.
- The first run succeeded with 0 alerts.
- I added no actions (notifications), since you didn't ask for one. Attaching a connector would be a follow-up.

The rule evaluates the last 5 minutes of real time. The sample data's timestamps are spread across Sep–Nov, so it is unlikely to fire on this dataset unless new 5xx documents arrive.

I created both objects through the API and checked them by reading them back. I did not check the dashboard's rendering in the browser. The temporary request files are in the scratchpad directory.
